subject: Discovery: Logging, retention, and PII redaction constraints
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@novushealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovusHealth Security <sec@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + security questionnaire (logging & PII)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the 30-minute intro earlier — Mark and I appreciated the quick demo of the routing and caching behavior. We wanted to capture the constraints we mentioned so you have them in one place. High level:

- We cannot persist any user-identifiable content in logs longer than 7 days without explicit consent.
- Audit logs (who/when/which model version) must be retained for 12 months and exportable for quarterly audits.
- All records that might contain PII need an automated redaction step before storage; we prefer server-side redaction over client-side.
- Any request/response pairs used for evals must be treated as PII unless redacted.

I've attached our security questionnaire (novus_security_ques_v2.pdf) and a short spreadsheet for the mutual action plan. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports:

1) Per-customer short-term token retention (7 days) with longer audit logs separate?
2) Automatic PII redaction hooks in the ingest pipeline (we use a custom proxy today)?
3) Exportable audit log format (CSV/JSON) with role-based access controls?

Next steps from our side: Mark will follow up with a paragraph on where logs flow in our infra so you can map gaps. We'd like a written recap from Redwood of the proposed safeguards and a rough estimate of effort for a Private deployment (VPC) vs Hosted with additional controls.

Thanks — Emma

Emma Li
Head of Privacy & Compliance
NovusHealth

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + security questionnaire (logging & PII)

Emma / Mark — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciate the attachments; I pulled the questionnaire and started a gap table. Below is a concise recap of what we heard on the call, plus our initial mapping to Redwood capabilities and suggested next steps.

Call recap (pain points & success criteria)
- Pain: Need to prevent storage of identifiable content (7-day retention) while still meeting audit obligations (12 months).
- Pain: Redaction must be deterministic and repeatable (server-side preferred).
- Success criteria: Ability to demonstrate exported audit logs for audits, show redaction in pipeline, and avoid model-quality regressions after redaction.

Current Novus stack (as stated)
- Ingress: Custom proxy that can mutate requests before forwarding.
- Serving: Mix of hosted endpoints and sandboxed on-prem infra for sensitive workloads.
- Logging: Centralized ELK cluster; currently stores request/response for 90 days.

Redwood mapping (short answers)
1) Per-customer short-term token retention: YES — Redwood supports configurable token/interaction retention windows per tenant. We can set ephemeral request bodies to 7 days while keeping immutable audit metadata for 12 months.
2) Automatic PII redaction hooks: PARTIAL — Redwood supports server-side pre-processing hooks (Lambda-style) where you can run redaction before persistence. We also have built-in regex-based redactors and a ML-based redaction addon (requires evaluation on your data).
3) Exportable audit logs: YES — audit logs can be exported as JSON/CSV via our Console or programmatically; RBAC controls are available in Private and Dedicated modes.

Open questions we need from you to size the work
- Can you share an example of the current log format and a sample redaction rule set? (Mark mentioned you'd send this.)
- How many distinct tenants/environments need the 7-day policy vs standard 90-day?
- Is Novus OK with Redwood running redaction in our control plane (hosted) or do you require the redaction step inside your VPC?

Proposed next steps
- Sofia: produce a short tech note mapping Redwood controls to each questionnaire item (target: EOD Sep 16).
- Jordan: provide pricing delta for Private vs Hosted with the required controls (target: Sep 17).
- Novus: Mark to send sample log snippets and confirm the number of tenants (target: Sep 15).

Attachments referenced: I attached a one-pager (inlined below) that enumerates the redaction options and where they run (control plane vs customer VPC). Let us know if you want a quick follow-up call this week.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake (Account Executive)

Sofia — quick add from my side so you have exacts for sizing:

- Log retention: We currently store full request/response pairs for 90 days but are contractually constrained to limit identifiable content (user name, SSN, email addresses, medical identifiers) to 7 days. Non-identifiable metadata (model id, request id, timestamp, user id hash) can live for 12 months.
- Redaction expectations: We prefer redaction to be implemented before logs hit ELK. That means either at the proxy or at the first point of ingress in Redwood.
- Audit exports: For SOC readiness we need quarterly exports of audit logs in JSON with the ability to map to internal user IDs (hashed).

Also: attaching the short diagram Emma mentioned (sent to you via Drive link) and a sample log line below for clarity.

Sample log (redactible fields in <>):
{"timestamp":"2026-09-14T14:51:12Z","request_id":"req_4b2e","user_id_hash":"h_7a9f","prompt":"Doctor, the patient <Name> reports...","model":"open-lr-7b","response":"..."}

That sample should make clear which fields we require redacted prior to persistence. Thanks for mapping options.

-Mark

- Option B (Private / VPC): 5 infra days for deployment + 4 SRE days for in-VPC redaction pipeline and HAC testing; higher monthly fee.
